title: ADVeRL-ELF: ADVersarial ELF Malware Generation using Reinforcement Learning
problem: Deep learning malware detection models are pervasive but lack robustness analysis against adversarial attacks; Linux-based malware adversarial generation is under-investigated despite the critical importance of hardening detection systems.
motivation: As ML models dominate malware detection, understanding their adversarial vulnerabilities is essential for security; systematic adversarial testing is rare for Linux ELF binaries.
method: The system uses reinforcement learning—an AI technique where an agent learns by taking actions and receiving rewards—to create adversarial (disguised) versions of Linux malware. It does this by adding NOPs (no-operation instructions that do nothing) into the running code in patterns that confuse malware detectors. These extra instructions don't change what the malware does—it keeps its original behavior intact. Over time, the AI learns which NOP placement patterns best hide the malware from detection.
key_novelty: Using reinforcement learning to generate Linux malware that evades detection by strategically injecting harmless no-operation instructions while preserving the malware's original functionality.
contributions: First RL framework for generating adversarial Linux ELF malware
Semantic NOP injection technique maintaining binary functionality while evading detection
59.5% attack success rate demonstrating significant vulnerabilities
Foundation for hardening Linux malware detection systems
baselines: baseline deep learning malware detection models
limitations: Evaluation limited to binary modification via NOP insertion; generalization to other adversarial techniques and modern defenses not discussed.
primary_theme: RL-driven adversarial malware generation for testing Linux detector robustness
